THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 21.08.2019 passed in MVC No.5307/2017 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 01.06.2017 petitioner was moving from Nelagadaranahalli to D.B.Kallu near HMT Layout Park, Bangalore on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-04 EK-2910 and at about 3.30 p.m., a car bearing registration No.KA-03 AC-6665 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with respondent No.2-insurance company dashed against his motor cycle.
Because of which, petitioner suffered fracture of left leg both bones, fracture of left 5th rib and simple injuries all over the body.

Hence, he filed MVC No.5307/2017.
4.

The Tribunal based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.1,74,893/- along with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit under the following heads:-
1. Pain and agony Rs.50,000/- Loss of income during laid 2. Rs.60,000/-

Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
5. The accident occurred in the year 2017.
Petitioner was aged 56 years at the time of accident and he was working as an electric contractor.
The treated doctor has deposed that petitioner suffered 34% disability to the left lower limb and whole body disability of 11%.

However, evidence of the injured P.W.1 reveals that there has been no loss of income due to the said disability and that the petitioner has been earning similar to what he was earning prior to the accident.
So, on the ground that there has been no functional disability, Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head of loss of future income.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'pain and agony', Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/-.
In my opinion, given the nature of injuries I deem the same to be appropriate.

Towards 'loss of income during laid up period',
Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/-.
This in my opinion is on the lower side.
Petitioner has produced his tax returns for the year 2015-16, which shows that he had paid tax on Rs.3,03,970/-.
Keeping his income at Rs.3,00,000/- annually, his monthly income would come to Rs.25,000/-.

Given the nature of injuries and the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that five months has to be considered as laid up period and towards 'loss of income during laid up period' petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- (Rs.25,000/- X 5) as against Rs.60,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards 'medical expenses', a sum of Rs.24,893/- is awarded.
As the same is based on the actual bills submitted, I deem it appropriate.
Towards 'loss of amenities and nutritious food' a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
In my opinion, given the nature of injuries, it would be appropriate to enhance it to a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
Towards 'attendance charges and conveyance' a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
I deem it just and appropriate.
Towards 'future medical expenses' a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded.
I deem the same to be appropriate.

Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads is modified as hereunder:-
1. Pain and agony Rs.50,000/-

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,59,893/- as against Rs.1,74,893/- as awarded by the Tribunal.

ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.85,000/- over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal;
iii) Respondent No.2-insurance company shall be liable to pay the enhanced compensation amount along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order;
iv) Draw modified award accordingly;
v) Registry to return the records to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.
